newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rights group accuses Chad of "kill" order.
newsitem.headline: French rights group accuses Chad of "kill" order.

text.p: A Paris-based international human rights group released on Friday a document it said was issued by authorities in the central African state of Chad, ordering police to shoot robbers on sight if they were caught in the act.
The document, said to be an order from the headquarters of the paramilitary national gendarmerie to field units, warned that officers who failed to obey could be sacked.

"We remind you once again that robbers must not be the object of normal procedures (of arrest). If one is caught in the act, you must immediately proceed with his physical elimination," the order said.
"Non-application of this order will result in very severe punishment including possible loss of rank and sacking from the force," it said.

The document was released by the International Federation of Human Rights Leagues (FIDH) which said its Chad affiliate had noted several cases of summary executions following the issuing of the order in November.

It said a pregnant woman suspected of stealing grain in a market was shot dead on the spot by gendarmes on November 16 and a boy was put in a bag and shot dead on the banks of the Chari river in similar circumstances two days earlier.
Three suspected livestock thieves were shot in public on December 26 while a man accused of stealing a container of oil was shot dead on December 15, the group said.
FIDH said the Chad authorities openly acknowledged having given the order on the grounds that the country's justice system was "inefficient and corrupt".
FIDH denounced "the responsibility of Chad authorities at the highest level...and questioned the value of the training given for many years by France to the Chad national gendarmerie."
